colors.name: Parchment Cream
colors.role: Page canvas and primary card surface - the warm off-white that defines Slite's identity. Never use cold white #ffffff at the page level

colors.name: Star White
colors.role: Elevated surfaces - product mockup cards, tooltips, white-product interiors stacked on top of the cream canvas

colors.name: Dust Sand
colors.role: Secondary surface and tag/chip background - a half-step darker than the canvas. Tag pills, secondary buttons, and warm-emphasis callouts

colors.name: Moon Silver
colors.role: Hairline borders, dividers, and 2px outlined button borders - the only border tone used at full opacity

colors.name: Shade Ink
colors.role: Primary heading and body text - slightly warm near-black. The headline color

colors.name: Shade Charcoal
colors.role: Secondary body text, navigation labels, and subdued headings. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

colors.name: Shade Slate
colors.role: Tertiary body text, captions, helper copy - the quietest readable gray

colors.name: Shade Fog
colors.role: Disabled states, placeholder text, and the lightest non-white neutral - used sparingly on the page

colors.name: Shade Dusk
colors.role: Small print and fine print text - pricing footnotes, micro-copy beneath headings

colors.name: Border Mist
colors.role: Card borders and stroke at low contrast - slightly bluer than Moon Silver, used when a card edge needs to be felt but not seen

colors.name: Ember Orange
colors.role: Primary action - filled CTA buttons, selected card border accent, featured testimonial card background, and the scribble-annotation color. The single saturated brand color, used sparingly so it always feels like a deliberate highlight

colors.name: Neptune Blue
colors.role: Secondary action accent - used on at most one button per page (e.g. alternating testimonial CTA) and link-text accents. Never the primary CTA

colors.name: Verification Green
colors.role: Green text accent for links, tags, and emphasized short phrases. Use as a supporting accent, not as a status color

colors.name: Verified Mint
colors.role: Green decorative accent for icons, marks, and small graphic details. Use as a supporting accent, not as a status color

colors.name: Tag Violet
colors.role: Violet text accent for links, tags, and emphasized short phrases. Use as a supporting accent, not as a status color

colors.name: Illustration Violet
colors.role: Decorative illustration fill - light-violet shapes in product mockups, paired with Tag Violet as a tonal pair

fonts.name: Garnett
fonts.role: Display and editorial headings. Used at 64px (display), 36px (h1), 28px (h2), 24px (large body), 12px (small links). The serif-like Garnett paired with a humanist sans is Slite's signature typographic contrast - it makes the page feel like a designed document rather than a dashboard.

fonts.name: UniversalSans
fonts.role: Body text, UI controls, navigation, buttons, and supporting headlines. Carries almost all of the page's content. The 50px / weight 400 / line-height 1.5 hero variant is a deliberate departure from typical 700-weight display sizes - it lets the Garnett headline above do the work, while UniversalSans handles the breathing paragraph copy beneath.

components.name: Primary CTA Button (Ember Pill)
components.role: The single orange button on the page - reserved for the main conversion action.

components.name: Dark CTA Button (Charcoal Pill)
components.role: Secondary high-emphasis action, typically 'Start for free'.

components.name: Outlined Pill Button
components.role: Medium-emphasis action - Book demo, secondary nav actions.

components.name: Ghost Text Button
components.role: Low-emphasis inline action - nav items, sub-actions inside cards.

components.name: Square Ghost Button
components.role: Compact UI control - close buttons, icon toggles, inline editors.

components.name: Dust Tag Chip
components.role: Feature highlight tags and category labels - the most-repeated component on the page.

components.name: Status Pill (Verified / Self-maintained)
components.role: Trust and maintenance indicators inside product screenshots.

components.name: Cream Feature Card
components.role: Primary marketing card - 3-column feature grid items, testimonial cards.

components.name: White Product Card
components.role: Product screenshot containers and tooltips stacked on the cream canvas.

components.name: Compact UI Card
components.role: Inline product UI mock elements - sidebar items, list rows, agent chips.

components.name: Ember Testimonial Card
components.role: Featured customer quote - the only orange-filled card.

components.name: Logo Trust Bar
components.role: Social proof - '3,000+ companies trust Slite' row.

components.name: Scribble Annotation
components.role: Hand-drawn circle or underline around a key word in a headline.

components.name: Hero Product Frame
components.role: Large product screenshot shown below the headline.

do: Set the page canvas to #fdf9f4 - never use cold white #ffffff as the page background
Use #f67748 for exactly one filled CTA per section; everything else is charcoal, outlined, or ghost
Use Garnett for headlines and UniversalSans for body - never use UniversalSans at 40px+ display sizes
Set button border-radius to 999px (pill) for all primary actions, 8px only for tiny square icon buttons
Set card border-radius to 32px for marketing cards, 12-18px for product mockup containers
Use #f9efe4 dust backgrounds for tag chips and secondary surfaces, not solid gray
Hand-draw a 1.5px #f67748 circle or underline around exactly one key word in any hero headline
doNot: Do not introduce a second saturated color as a brand accent - #f67748 must remain the only chromatic surface color
Do not use 700-weight UniversalSans at display sizes - 50px hero text is always weight 400
Do not stack more than one shadow elevation on a single element; the three-layer shadow is the maximum
Do not use pure black #000000 for body text - always #2d2f34 (Shade Ink) or #3f434a (Shade Charcoal)
Do not use #ecedef or #d9dde6 as background fills - these are border tones only
Do not break the pill/tag radius system with square chips or rounded-but-not-pill buttons
Do not place #f67748 fills on large backgrounds (more than 20% of a section) - it dilutes the CTA signal
